text: The Supreme Court in the landmark case of Kesavananda Bharati vs. State of Kerala (1973) held that
options: Parliament can amend any part of the Constitution
Parliament cannot amend any part of the Constitution
The President has the power to amend the Constitution
The Judiciary has the power to amend the Constitution
correctAnswer: Parliament can amend any part of the Constitution
explanation: The Supreme Court in the landmark case of Kesavananda Bharati vs. State of Kerala (1973) held that Parliament has the power to amend any part of the Constitution, except the basic structure.

text: The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India is responsible for
options: Auditing the accounts of the Union Government
Auditing the accounts of the State Governments
Auditing the accounts of both the Union and State Governments
Auditing the accounts of the Supreme Court
correctAnswer: Auditing the accounts of both the Union and State Governments
explanation: The CAG of India is responsible for auditing the accounts of both the Union and State Governments, as well as the autonomous bodies and public undertakings.
